notes: Sampling predicate fires (415 % 5 == 0), but zero findings were posted at all (no review, only the routine dependency-review bot comment) — zero valid-finding denominator makes the settled state n/a, not completed/never-run, so no subagent was dispatched for literally nothing to review. **2026-08-15 /maintenance staleness sweep.** This record's null `reviewInterval` was re-checked and is retained, but the reason was nearly recorded wrong. The sweep first read "no Codex comment" as "never reviewed"; the PR in fact carries exactly one 👍 reaction and nothing else, which is the connector's own documented clean-pass signal ("If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍"). Reaction authorship is not exposed by the GitHub access available here, so this is strong evidence rather than proof — but the timing agrees (see below), and this record's original note already read it as a silent clean pass, which was correct. **The measurement consequence is real either way:** `loop-metrics.mjs` counts `**Reviewed commit:**` markers, and a 👍-only pass emits none, so a clean review is indistinguishable from no review in the mechanical half. That is a second blind spot alongside the review-body findings gap recorded on #447. Numbers left as derived rather than hand-corrected, per the never-type-mechanical-values rule. Open 61 minutes, ample time for a pass (PR #443 fit six rounds into 162).
